name: Waving-Z
statusNote: Small C++11 codebase whose only library dependency is Boost, with no GNU Radio or Python; last code change 2018-06-14 and a typo fix on 2022-04-03. G.9959 (01/2015) is still the edition in force.
note: An ITU-T G.9959 (de)modulator for Z-Wave (started as a fork of andersesbensen/rtl-zwave). `wave-in` decodes Z-Wave frames from a raw I/Q stream piped in from an RTL-SDR (`rtl_sdr`) or HackRF; `wave-out` encodes frames and transmits them through `hackrf_transfer`. The rtl_433-style entry point for getting Z-Wave packets off a cheap SDR.

name: rtl-zwave
statusNote: Code unchanged since 2015-03-18; the only later commit (2023-09-17) added LICENSE.md. It demodulates the G.9959 FSK rates (9.6/40/100 kbps; G.9959 01/2015 is still the edition in force) and has no support for the DSSS-OQPSK Z-Wave Long Range PHY.
note: The original G.9959 (Z-Wave) demodulator for the RTL-SDR: pipe `rtl_sdr` samples into it and it prints decoded Z-Wave frames. Lightweight, receive-only, and the codebase Waving-Z grew out of, a minimal way to confirm Z-Wave traffic and read frame headers on a ~$30 dongle.

name: EZ-Wave
statusNote: The original AFITWiSec/EZ-Wave GitHub repository now returns 404; what remains is a copy under another account whose last commit is dated 2016-01-17. Its README requires Python 2.7 and GNU Radio 3.7+ and says it was tested on Ubuntu 14.04 only.
note: The reference open Z-Wave assessment suite (GNU Radio + Scapy-radio): ezstumbler does passive discovery and active network enumeration, ezrecon interrogates a device (manufacturer/model, firmware version, supported command classes, configuration), and ezfingerprint identifies the Z-Wave module generation via a PHY preamble-length manipulation. Default config drives two HackRF One SDRs. Python 2.7 / GNU Radio 3.7 era, dated but still the canonical exploitation toolkit.

name: Scapy-radio
statusNote: Installs with python2 and requires GNU Radio 3.7 per its README and install.sh; last commit 2016-04-01. No package on PyPI or in Debian.
note: GNU Radio flowgraphs plus a patched Scapy that lets you sniff, dissect, craft and replay several sub-GHz/2.4 GHz protocols, including a Z-Wave layer, straight from a Python/Scapy session over an SDR (HackRF). The radio/Scapy plumbing EZ-Wave builds on, and a standalone way to script Z-Wave frame capture and injection.

name: gr-zwave_poore
statusNote: Upstream has had no commit since 2022-08-28, but FISSURE pulls it in as a git submodule and its installers build it on Ubuntu, Kali, DragonOS, Raspberry Pi OS, Parrot and BackBox. The default maint-3.10 branch is for GNU Radio 3.10 and later.
note: A GNU Radio out-of-tree module that transmits (and helps decode) Z-Wave signals, tested with a USRP B210; integrated into AINFOSEC's FISSURE RF framework. Branches for GNU Radio 3.7/3.8/3.10. A GNU Radio block path for Z-Wave TX when you want a flowgraph rather than the Scapy-radio stack.

name: Z-Wave Zniffer
note: Silicon Labs' official GUI tool (in Simplicity Studio) that captures RF communication on a Z-Wave network for debugging, the vendor sniffer. Decodes the full Z-Wave frame including command classes and shows security (S0/S2) handshakes. Needs a USB Z-Wave adapter flashed with Zniffer firmware (e.g. a UZB stick). The turnkey capture path when an SDR demod is too fiddly.

name: Z-Wave PC Controller
note: Silicon Labs' official GUI controller (Simplicity Studio): implements a Z-Wave controller node over the Serial API of a UZB USB adapter, so you can include/exclude nodes, browse the device's supported command classes and send them, driving a Z-Wave network legitimately from a PC. The application-layer counterpart to the Zniffer's capture.

name: Silicon Labs UZB-7 Z-Wave 700 Stick (SLUSB001A)
spec: EFR32ZG14 Z-Wave 700 SoC · Serial API over USB (CP2102N VCOM) · firmware-upgradeable
note: Silicon Labs' EFR32ZG14 USB stick that exposes the Z-Wave Serial API to a host, the controller adapter the Z-Wave PC Controller drives, and (re-flashed with Zniffer firmware) the capture adapter for the Z-Wave Zniffer. The official native-radio hardware for both vendor tools, ~US$21.
